d3f:AssetInventory.obligationLabel: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
d3f:AssetInventory.rationale: Asset management in (i) starts from knowing what the assets are, which is what this technique produces.

d3f:AuthenticationEventThresholding.rationale: Incident handling in (b) presupposes detection. Thresholding authentication events is one detection input, not a handling process.

d3f:CredentialRotation.obligationLabel: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
d3f:CredentialRotation.rationale: Rotating credentials is credential lifecycle management, which sits under the access-control limb of (i) without being what the point asks for.

d3f:DiskEncryption.obligationLabel: Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data
d3f:DiskEncryption.rationale: Article 32(1)(a) offers encryption as an example measure. Disk encryption protects data at rest against loss of the medium only, and does nothing for the pseudonymisation limb of the same point.

d3f:EncryptedTunnels.obligationLabel: Policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption
d3f:EncryptedTunnels.rationale: A tunnel protects the channel rather than the message, so it evidences use of cryptography without saying anything about the data at either end.

d3f:FileEncryption.obligationLabel: Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data
d3f:FileEncryption.rationale: Encrypting the files that hold personal data addresses the encryption limb of (a) directly, at a granularity a controller can point at.

d3f:MessageEncryption.obligationLabel: Policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption
d3f:MessageEncryption.rationale: Covers the cryptography-in-transit half of (h). The policies-and-procedures half is organisational and no diagram can assert it.

d3f:Multi-factorAuthentication.obligationLabel: Multi-factor or continuous authentication, secured voice, video and text communications and secured emergency communication systems
d3f:Multi-factorAuthentication.rationale: Article 21(2)(j) names multi-factor authentication in as many words; the D3FEND technique is the same control.

d3f:NetworkVulnerabilityAssessment.obligationLabel: Process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of the measures
d3f:NetworkVulnerabilityAssessment.rationale: Regular assessment of the measures' effectiveness is what (d) requires; this technique tests the network measures specifically.

d3f:RestoreDatabase.obligationLabel: Ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident
d3f:RestoreDatabase.rationale: Article 32(1)(c) asks for the ability to restore availability and access. Restoring the database that holds the personal data is that ability; whether it happens in a timely manner is not something the diagram states.

d3f:RestoreDiskImage.obligationLabel: Business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management
d3f:RestoreDiskImage.rationale: Restoring an image is the recovery half of (c). Backup management and crisis management are separate duties in the same point.

d3f:SoftwareUpdate.obligationLabel: Security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure
d3f:SoftwareUpdate.rationale: Applying updates is how a handled vulnerability stops being one, so it evidences the maintenance limb of (e).

d3f:StrongPasswordPolicy.obligationLabel: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
d3f:StrongPasswordPolicy.rationale: Speaks to the access-control limb of (i). Human resources security and asset management are elsewhere in the same point and untouched by it.

d3f:SystemVulnerabilityAssessment.obligationLabel: Security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure
d3f:SystemVulnerabilityAssessment.rationale: Vulnerability handling in (e) begins with finding them. Disclosure, and security during acquisition and development, are not addressed.

d3f:UserAccountPermissions.obligationLabel: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
d3f:UserAccountPermissions.rationale: Per-account permissions are the enforcement point an access control policy is written for; the policy itself is organisational.
